blocks.en: The King Over the Waters
blocks.es_reference: El Rey Sobre las Aguas

blocks.en: These five chapters carry the King from Galilee toward Jerusalem, and at their center stands the confession on which He says He will build His church. They open with two great signs over the sea. After feeding five thousand from five loaves and two fish, Jesus sends the disciples ahead in the boat and comes to them walking on the water. Peter asks to come, steps out, and for a moment walks on the waves — until he sees the wind, is afraid, and begins to sink, crying, "Lord, save me!" Jesus catches him: "O you of little faith, why did you doubt?" (Matthew 14:31). When He climbs into the boat and the wind ceases, the disciples worship Him, saying, "Truly You are the Son of God" (Matthew 14:33). Here is the question of the whole unit already taking shape — who is this? — and the first stammering answer from the men closest to Him.
blocks.es_reference: Estos cinco capítulos llevan al Rey desde Galilea hacia Jerusalén, y en su centro está la confesión sobre la cual dice que edificará su iglesia. Comienzan con dos grandes señales sobre el mar. Después de alimentar a cinco mil con cinco panes y dos peces, Jesús envía a los discípulos delante en la barca y viene a ellos andando sobre el agua. Pedro pide venir, sale, y por un momento anda sobre las olas — hasta que ve el viento, tiene miedo y comienza a hundirse, clamando: "¡Señor, sálvame!" Jesús lo toma: "Hombre de poca fe, ¿por qué dudaste?" (Mateo 14:31). Cuando sube a la barca y el viento cesa, los discípulos le adoran, diciendo: "Verdaderamente eres Hijo de Dios" (Mateo 14:33). Aquí ya toma forma la pregunta de toda la unidad — ¿quién es éste? — y la primera respuesta balbuciente de los hombres más cercanos a Él.

blocks.en: What Defiles, and a Great Faith
blocks.es_reference: Lo Que Contamina, y una Gran Fe

blocks.en: In chapter 15 the King corrects the Pharisees over their traditions. They were scandalized that His disciples ate with unwashed hands, but Jesus turns the matter inside out: "Not what goes into the mouth defiles a man; but what comes out of the mouth, this defiles a man" (Matthew 15:11). For "out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries" and the rest (Matthew 15:19). Defilement is not a matter of ceremony but of the heart. Then comes a Gentile woman of Canaan, begging Him to heal her demon-tormented daughter. Jesus seems at first to refuse, testing her, but she presses on with humble persistence, and He marvels: "O woman, great is your faith! Let it be to you as you desire" (Matthew 15:28). As with the centurion earlier, it is an outsider who shows the faith the King seeks, another sign that His church will gather people from every nation.
blocks.es_reference: En el capítulo 15 el Rey corrige a los fariseos sobre sus tradiciones. Se escandalizaban de que sus discípulos comieran con manos sin lavar, pero Jesús vuelve el asunto al revés: "No lo que entra en la boca contamina al hombre; mas lo que sale de la boca, esto contamina al hombre" (Mateo 15:11). Porque "del corazón salen los malos pensamientos, los homicidios, los adulterios" y lo demás (Mateo 15:19). La contaminación no es cuestión de ceremonia sino del corazón. Luego viene una mujer gentil de Canaán, rogándole que sane a su hija atormentada por un demonio. Jesús parece al principio negarse, probándola, pero ella insiste con humilde persistencia, y Él se maravilla: "Oh mujer, grande es tu fe; sea hecho contigo como quieres" (Mateo 15:28). Como con el centurión antes, es una extraña quien muestra la fe que el Rey busca, otra señal de que su iglesia reunirá gente de toda nación.

blocks.en: The Great Confession
blocks.es_reference: La Gran Confesión

blocks.en: At Caesarea Philippi the King asks the question directly. First, "Who do men say that the Son of Man is?" The answers are flattering but wrong — John the Baptist, Elijah, Jeremiah, one of the prophets. Then He turns it on them: "But who do you say that I am?" Peter answers for them all: "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God" (Matthew 16:16). Jesus calls him blessed, "for flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but My Father who is in heaven" (Matthew 16:17). This is the heart of the whole Gospel. No one comes to this confession by his own cleverness or by hearsay; it is given by God. And on this confession the King makes His great promise: "You are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it" (Matthew 16:18). There is a play on words here — Peter (Petros) means a small stone, while the rock (petra) on which the church is built is the bedrock of the Spirit-given truth Peter has just confessed: that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God. The church is not built on a man, but on Christ confessed. And the gates of Hades — gates being a defensive thing — will not hold out against it; the church is meant to advance, and hell's defenses will not stand. To His people the King gives the keys of the kingdom, the authority to open its doors by the gospel.
blocks.es_reference: En Cesarea de Filipo el Rey hace la pregunta directamente. Primero: "¿Quién dicen los hombres que es el Hijo del Hombre?" Las respuestas son halagadoras pero erradas — Juan el Bautista, Elías, Jeremías, uno de los profetas. Luego la vuelve hacia ellos: "Y vosotros, ¿quién decís que soy yo?" Pedro responde por todos: "Tú eres el Cristo, el Hijo del Dios viviente" (Mateo 16:16). Jesús lo llama bienaventurado, "porque no te lo reveló carne ni sangre, sino mi Padre que está en los cielos" (Mateo 16:17). Este es el corazón de todo el Evangelio. Nadie llega a esta confesión por su propia astucia ni de oídas; es dada por Dios. Y sobre esta confesión el Rey hace su gran promesa: "Tú eres Pedro, y sobre esta roca edificaré mi iglesia; y las puertas del Hades no prevalecerán contra ella" (Mateo 16:18). Hay aquí un juego de palabras: Pedro (Petros) significa una piedra pequeña, mientras que la roca (petra) sobre la cual se edifica la iglesia es la roca firme de la verdad dada por el Espíritu que Pedro acaba de confesar: que Jesús es el Cristo, el Hijo del Dios viviente. La iglesia no se edifica sobre un hombre, sino sobre Cristo confesado. Y las puertas del Hades — siendo las puertas algo defensivo — no resistirán contra ella; la iglesia ha de avanzar, y las defensas del infierno no se mantendrán en pie. A su pueblo el Rey le da las llaves del reino, la autoridad de abrir sus puertas por el evangelio.

blocks.en: The Cross Foretold
blocks.es_reference: La Cruz Anunciada

blocks.en: From this high point the King turns at once toward the cross. "From that time Jesus began to show His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem, and suffer many things... and be killed, and be raised the third day" (Matthew 16:21). Peter, who had just confessed so rightly, now rebukes Him — surely this must never happen — and Jesus answers with startling sharpness, "Get behind Me, Satan! You are an offense to Me, for you are not mindful of the things of God but the things of men" (Matthew 16:23). The same Peter can be the voice of revelation one moment and the voice of the tempter the next. Then the King lays down the law of discipleship once more: "If anyone desires to come after Me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow Me. For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will find it" (Matthew 16:24-25). The church is founded on a confessed Christ who is going to die, and to follow Him is to take up a cross too.
blocks.es_reference: Desde este punto alto el Rey se vuelve enseguida hacia la cruz. "Desde entonces comenzó Jesús a declarar a sus discípulos que le era necesario ir a Jerusalén y padecer mucho... y ser muerto, y resucitar al tercer día" (Mateo 16:21). Pedro, que acababa de confesar tan correctamente, ahora lo reprende — seguramente esto nunca debe suceder — y Jesús responde con sorprendente aspereza: "¡Quítate de delante de mí, Satanás!; me eres tropiezo, porque no pones la mira en las cosas de Dios, sino en las de los hombres" (Mateo 16:23). El mismo Pedro puede ser la voz de la revelación en un momento y la voz del tentador al siguiente. Luego el Rey establece de nuevo la ley del discipulado: "Si alguno quiere venir en pos de mí, niéguese a sí mismo, y tome su cruz, y sígame. Porque todo el que quiera salvar su vida, la perderá; y todo el que pierda su vida por causa de mí, la hallará" (Mateo 16:24-25). La iglesia se funda sobre un Cristo confesado que va a morir, y seguirle es tomar también una cruz.

blocks.en: True Discipleship: Deny, Take Up, Follow
blocks.es_reference: El Verdadero Discipulado: Negarse, Tomar la Cruz, Seguir

blocks.en: A sermon from Matthew 16:21-26 organizes Jesus' call with three plain verbs: a true disciple denies himself, takes up his cross, and follows Christ. Self-denial is not self-mutilation or giving up something we never wanted in the first place. It means renouncing the throne of the self so that Christ is first. F. B. Meyer once pictured surrender as giving Christ the keys to every room of life; one locked room still meant an unsurrendered house. Taking up the cross is likewise more specific than enduring ordinary trouble. A cross is suffering that comes from doing the will of God. Finally, following Christ means walking in His steps rather than asking Him to approve a path we have already chosen. Peter's protest in this passage shows how easy it is to want a Messiah without a cross and discipleship without self-denial. Jesus will not permit that separation. The road of the King and the road of His disciple meet at the same place: "not my will," the surrender of self, and faithful obedience to God.
blocks.es_reference: Un sermón sobre Mateo 16:21-26 organiza el llamado de Jesús con tres verbos sencillos: el verdadero discípulo se niega a sí mismo, toma su cruz y sigue a Cristo. Negarse a uno mismo no significa mutilarse ni renunciar a algo que nunca deseábamos. Significa renunciar al trono del yo para que Cristo ocupe el primer lugar. F. B. Meyer ilustró una vez la entrega como dar a Cristo las llaves de cada habitación de la vida; una habitación cerrada todavía significaba una casa no entregada por completo. Tomar la cruz también es algo más específico que soportar las dificultades comunes. Una cruz es sufrimiento que viene por hacer la voluntad de Dios. Finalmente, seguir a Cristo significa andar en Sus pisadas en vez de pedirle que apruebe un camino que ya hemos escogido. La protesta de Pedro en este pasaje muestra cuán fácil es querer un Mesías sin cruz y un discipulado sin negación propia. Jesús no permite esa separación. El camino del Rey y el camino de Su discípulo se encuentran en el mismo lugar: «no mi voluntad», la rendición del yo y la obediencia fiel a Dios.

blocks.en: Glory on the Mountain
blocks.es_reference: Gloria en el Monte

blocks.en: Six days later He takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain and is transfigured before them, His face shining like the sun. Moses and Elijah — the law and the prophets — appear and talk with Him. Peter wants to build three tabernacles, but a bright cloud overshadows them, and the Father's voice repeats the word spoken at the Jordan, now with a command added: "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Hear Him!" (Matthew 17:5). The glory confirms the confession: this truly is the Son of God, and He, not Moses or Elijah, is the One to be heard. Coming down, they fail to heal an epileptic boy, and Jesus teaches that even faith as small as a mustard seed can move mountains (Matthew 17:20). The chapter ends with another quiet sign of who He is, as a coin to pay the temple tax is found in the mouth of a fish.
blocks.es_reference: Seis días después toma a Pedro, Jacobo y Juan a un monte alto y es transfigurado delante de ellos, resplandeciendo su rostro como el sol. Moisés y Elías — la ley y los profetas — aparecen y hablan con Él. Pedro quiere hacer tres enramadas, pero una nube de luz los cubre, y la voz del Padre repite la palabra dicha en el Jordán, ahora con un mandato añadido: "Éste es mi Hijo amado, en quien tengo contentamiento; a él oíd" (Mateo 17:5). La gloria confirma la confesión: éste es verdaderamente el Hijo de Dios, y a Él, no a Moisés ni a Elías, hay que oír. Al descender, no logran sanar a un muchacho epiléptico, y Jesús enseña que aun una fe tan pequeña como un grano de mostaza puede mover montañas (Mateo 17:20). El capítulo termina con otra señal callada de quién es Él, al hallarse en la boca de un pez la moneda para pagar el tributo del templo.

blocks.en: Who Is Greatest?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Quién Es el Mayor?

blocks.en: Chapter 18 is the fourth great discourse, and it is about life in the King's family, the church. The disciples ask who is greatest in the kingdom, and Jesus sets a little child among them: "Unless you are converted and become as little children, you will by no means enter the kingdom of heaven" (Matthew 18:3). Greatness in the church is not rank but the humility of a child. Then He gives a fierce warning against causing one of these little ones to stumble — better a millstone around the neck and the depths of the sea (Matthew 18:6). And He tells of the shepherd who leaves the ninety-nine to seek the one that wandered off, "for it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish" (Matthew 18:14). The church is to guard and seek its weakest members with the very heart of God.
blocks.es_reference: El capítulo 18 es el cuarto gran discurso, y trata de la vida en la familia del Rey, la iglesia. Los discípulos preguntan quién es el mayor en el reino, y Jesús pone a un niño en medio de ellos: "De cierto os digo, que si no os volvéis y os hacéis como niños, no entraréis en el reino de los cielos" (Mateo 18:3). La grandeza en la iglesia no es el rango sino la humildad de un niño. Luego da una severa advertencia contra hacer tropezar a uno de estos pequeños — mejor una piedra de molino al cuello y lo profundo del mar (Mateo 18:6). Y habla del pastor que deja las noventa y nueve para buscar la que se descarrió, "porque no es la voluntad de vuestro Padre que está en los cielos, que se pierda uno de estos pequeños" (Mateo 18:14). La iglesia ha de guardar y buscar a sus miembros más débiles con el mismísimo corazón de Dios.

blocks.en: The Way of the Church
blocks.es_reference: El Camino de la Iglesia

blocks.en: Jesus then gives the pattern for dealing with sin among His people. "If your brother sins against you, go and tell him his fault between you and him alone." If he will not hear, take one or two others; if he still will not hear, "tell it to the church" (Matthew 18:15-17). The goal at every step is to win the brother, not to expose him. To the church He gives a real authority to bind and to loose — to declare the terms of the gospel and to exercise loving discipline. And in the middle of this teaching on the gathered church comes one of the most precious promises in the Gospel: "For where two or three are gathered together in My name, I am there in the midst of them" (Matthew 18:20). The church does not need a great crowd to have its King present; He is there wherever even two or three gather in His name.
blocks.es_reference: Entonces Jesús da el patrón para tratar con el pecado entre su pueblo. "Si tu hermano peca contra ti, ve y repréndele estando tú y él solos." Si no oye, toma a uno o dos más; si todavía no oye, "dilo a la iglesia" (Mateo 18:15-17). La meta en cada paso es ganar al hermano, no exponerlo. A la iglesia le da una verdadera autoridad de atar y desatar — de declarar los términos del evangelio y de ejercer una disciplina amorosa. Y en medio de esta enseñanza sobre la iglesia reunida viene una de las promesas más preciosas del Evangelio: "Porque donde están dos o tres congregados en mi nombre, allí estoy yo en medio de ellos" (Mateo 18:20). La iglesia no necesita una gran multitud para tener presente a su Rey; Él está allí dondequiera que aun dos o tres se reúnan en su nombre.

blocks.en: Forgiveness Without Limit
blocks.es_reference: El Perdón Sin Límite

blocks.en: Peter asks how often he must forgive a brother — up to seven times? Jesus answers, "Up to seventy times seven" (Matthew 18:22), which is to say, without keeping count. Then He tells the parable of the unforgiving servant. A servant who owed his king an unpayable fortune was forgiven the whole debt out of mercy. But that same servant went out and seized a fellow servant who owed him a trifling sum, refusing him the very mercy he had just received, and had him thrown into prison. When the king heard, he delivered the wicked servant to the tormentors. The warning is plain: "So My heavenly Father also will do to you if each of you, from his heart, does not forgive his brother his trespasses" (Matthew 18:35). The church is a community of the forgiven, and those who have been forgiven so great a debt by God cannot clutch the small debts of others.
blocks.es_reference: Pedro pregunta cuántas veces debe perdonar a un hermano — ¿hasta siete? Jesús responde: "Hasta setenta veces siete" (Mateo 18:22), es decir, sin llevar la cuenta. Luego cuenta la parábola del siervo que no perdonó. Un siervo que debía a su rey una fortuna impagable fue perdonado de toda la deuda por misericordia. Pero ese mismo siervo salió y agarró a un consiervo que le debía una suma insignificante, negándole la misma misericordia que acababa de recibir, y lo hizo echar en la cárcel. Cuando el rey lo oyó, entregó al siervo malvado a los verdugos. La advertencia es clara: "Así también mi Padre celestial hará con vosotros si no perdonáis de todo corazón cada uno a su hermano sus ofensas" (Mateo 18:35). La iglesia es una comunidad de los perdonados, y los que han sido perdonados de tan gran deuda por Dios no pueden aferrarse a las pequeñas deudas de los demás.

blocks.en: The King and His Church
blocks.es_reference: El Rey y Su Iglesia

blocks.en: Put together, these chapters give us the King and the church He builds. The church rests on one foundation: the Spirit-given confession that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God. It is built by Him, not by us, and the gates of hell will not withstand it. Its King is going to the cross, and to belong to Him is to deny self and follow. And its common life is to look like its King: marked by childlike humility rather than rivalry, by tender care for the weak and straying, by honest and loving correction when sin appears, and by a forgiveness without limit that flows from having been forgiven an unpayable debt. Wherever two or three gather around that confession in His name, the King Himself is present, and His church goes forward against the very gates of hell.
blocks.es_reference: Reunidos, estos capítulos nos dan al Rey y a la iglesia que Él edifica. La iglesia descansa sobre un solo fundamento: la confesión dada por el Espíritu de que Jesús es el Cristo, el Hijo del Dios viviente. Es edificada por Él, no por nosotros, y las puertas del infierno no resistirán contra ella. Su Rey va a la cruz, y pertenecerle es negarse a sí mismo y seguirle. Y su vida común ha de parecerse a su Rey: marcada por la humildad de un niño en vez de la rivalidad, por el tierno cuidado de los débiles y descarriados, por la corrección honesta y amorosa cuando aparece el pecado, y por un perdón sin límite que brota de haber sido perdonados de una deuda impagable. Dondequiera que dos o tres se reúnen en torno a esa confesión en su nombre, el Rey mismo está presente, y su iglesia avanza contra las puertas mismas del infierno.

blocks.en: "For where two or three are gathered together in My name, I am there in the midst of them." — Matthew 18:20 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Porque donde están dos o tres congregados en mi nombre, allí estoy yo en medio de ellos." — Mateo 18:20 (RVG)

sa.prompt: Describe the walking on the water and what it reveals about Jesus and about Peter's faith.
sa.model: After feeding the five thousand, Jesus sent the disciples ahead and came to them walking on the water. Peter asked to come and for a moment was walking on the waves toward Jesus, but when he saw the wind he was afraid and began sinking, crying for the Lord to save him. Jesus caught him and said, O you of little faith, why did you doubt, showing that Peter walked while looking to Jesus but sank when fear took over. When Jesus climbed into the boat the wind ceased, and the disciples began to worship Him, saying truly You are the Son of God. The scene reveals Jesus as Lord over the water and already presses the question of who He is that the whole unit will answer.

sa.prompt: According to Jesus, what truly defiles a person, and why?
sa.model: When the Pharisees were scandalized that the disciples ate with unwashed hands, Jesus turned their tradition inside out and taught that what goes into the mouth does not defile a person, but what comes out of the mouth defiles him. He explained that the things which come out proceed from the heart, for out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, and the rest. So true defilement is not a matter of ceremony or ritual washing but of the heart inside. The Pharisees had focused on the outside while their hearts were unclean, and Jesus taught that the real problem in every person is the corrupt heart from which sin proceeds.

sa.prompt: Describe the faith of the Canaanite woman and what it shows about the King's church.
sa.model: A Gentile woman of Canaan came begging Jesus to heal her daughter, who was tormented by a demon. Jesus at first seemed to refuse, testing her, but she pressed on with humble persistence and would not be turned away. He marveled and said, O woman, great is your faith, and her daughter was healed from that hour. As with the centurion earlier in the Gospel, it is an outsider, a Gentile from beyond Israel, who shows the very faith the King is looking for. This shows that the King's church will not be limited to one nation but will gather people of great faith from every nation, an early sign of the worldwide church being built on the confession of Christ.

sa.prompt: What was Peter's great confession, and how did he come to know it?
sa.model: At Caesarea Philippi Jesus first asked who men said the Son of Man was, and the answers were John the Baptist, Elijah, or one of the prophets. Then He asked the disciples directly, and Peter confessed for them all, You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. Jesus called him blessed and said that flesh and blood had not revealed this to him, but His Father who is in heaven. So Peter did not come to this confession by his own cleverness or by hearsay; it was given to him by God. This is the heart of the whole Gospel, that no one truly confesses Jesus as the Christ and Son of God except by the revelation of the Father through the Spirit.

sa.prompt: Explain what 'on this rock I will build My church' means in this unit, and the promise about the gates of Hades.
sa.model: There is a play on words: Peter is Petros, a small stone, while the rock on which the church is built is petra, a bedrock. The lesson teaches that the rock is not the man Peter but the Spirit-given confession Peter had just made, that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God. So the church is built not on a man but on Christ confessed, and not by us but by Him. Jesus promised that the gates of Hades would not prevail against it. Since gates are a defensive structure, the picture is of the advancing church battering down the defenses of hell rather than barely holding out. The church is meant to go forward against the gates of hell, and they will not stand.

sa.prompt: After the confession, what did Jesus foretell, and what did He say it means to follow Him?
sa.model: From the time of the confession Jesus began to show the disciples that He must go to Jerusalem, suffer many things, be killed, and be raised the third day. When Peter rebuked Him, saying this must never happen, Jesus answered, Get behind Me, Satan, for Peter was minding the things of men and not of God. Then Jesus said that if anyone desires to come after Him he must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Him, for whoever would save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for Christ's sake will find it. So the church is founded on a confessed Christ who is going to the cross, and to follow Him is to take up a cross and lose one's life for His sake.

sa.prompt: Describe the Transfiguration and the word the Father spoke.
sa.model: Jesus took Peter, James, and John up a high mountain and was transfigured before them, His face shining like the sun. Moses and Elijah, representing the law and the prophets, appeared and talked with Him. Peter wanted to build three tabernacles, but a bright cloud overshadowed them and the Father's voice came, repeating the word spoken at the Jordan and adding a command: This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased, hear Him. The glory on the mountain confirmed Peter's confession, showing that this truly is the Son of God, and the Father's command made clear that Christ, and not Moses or Elijah, is the one to be heard. Coming down, Jesus taught that faith as small as a mustard seed can move mountains.

sa.prompt: What does chapter 18 teach about true greatness and about the little ones?
sa.model: When the disciples asked who is greatest in the kingdom, Jesus set a little child among them and said that unless they are converted and become like little children they will not enter the kingdom of heaven. Greatness in the church is not rank but the humility of a child. He then warned fiercely against causing one of these little ones to stumble, saying it would be better to have a millstone around the neck and be drowned in the sea. And He told of the shepherd who leaves the ninety-nine to seek the one sheep that wandered off, because it is not the will of the Father that one of these little ones should perish. So the church is to guard and seek its weakest and straying members with the very heart of God.

sa.prompt: What pattern did Jesus give for dealing with a sinning brother, and what did He promise about two or three gathered?
sa.model: Jesus gave a pattern for dealing with sin among His people. If a brother sins, the first step is to go and tell him his fault between the two of them alone; if he will not hear, take one or two others; and if he still will not hear, tell it to the church. The goal at every step is to win the brother back, not to expose him. To the church Jesus gave real authority to bind and to loose, to declare the terms of the gospel and to exercise loving correction and discipline. In the midst of this teaching He gave the precious promise that where two or three are gathered together in His name, He is present there in the midst of them. So the church does not need a great crowd to have its King present with it.

sa.prompt: Explain the parable of the unforgiving servant and how it gathers the unit's theme of the King and His church.
sa.model: When Peter asked how often to forgive, Jesus said up to seventy times seven, meaning without keeping count, and told of a servant forgiven an unpayable debt by his king out of mercy, who then seized a fellow servant owing a trifling sum and refused him the same mercy. The king delivered the wicked servant to the tormentors, and Jesus warned that the heavenly Father will do the same if we do not forgive our brother from the heart. This gathers the whole theme of the King and His church, for the church is built on the Spirit-given confession that Jesus is the Christ, and its common life is to look like its King: a community of the forgiven who, having been forgiven so great a debt, forgive others, and who live in childlike humility, care for the weak, and loving correction.
